title: Policies for information security
text: Management should define, approve, communicate, and review an information security policy in line with business requirements, relevant legislation, and regulation.

title: Information security roles and responsibilities
text: Information security roles and responsibilities are assigned and communicated to all personnel.

title: Segregation of duties
text: Conflicting duties and areas of responsibility are segregated to reduce opportunities for unauthorized or unintentional modification or misuse.

title: Management responsibilities
text: Management requires all employees and contractors to apply information security in line with the organization's established policy.

title: Contact with authorities
text: Appropriate contacts with relevant authorities are established and maintained to facilitate incident handling, legal issues, and coordination.

title: Contact with special interest groups
text: Contacts with special interest groups, security forums, and professional associations are established and maintained.

title: Threat intelligence
text: Information about threats relevant to the organization is collected, analyzed, and used to inform security decisions.

title: Information security in project management
text: Information security is integrated into project management to address risks within each project's lifecycle.

title: Inventory of information and other associated assets
text: An inventory of information and other associated assets is maintained, identifying owners and the approved handling rules for each asset.

title: Acceptable use of information and other associated assets
text: Rules for the acceptable use of information and associated assets are identified, documented, and implemented.

title: Return of assets
text: All information and associated assets are returned to the organization upon termination, change, or completion of employment, contract, or agreement.

title: Classification of information
text: Information is classified according to its value, legal requirements, sensitivity, and criticality to the organization.

title: Labelling of information
text: A set of procedures is developed and implemented for information labelling in line with the organization's classification scheme.

title: Information transfer
text: Rules, procedures, and agreements are in place to protect information transferred across communication and physical transport channels.

title: Access control
text: Rules for controlling physical and logical access to information and assets are established and enforced, based on business and security requirements.

title: Identity management
text: The full lifecycle of identities is managed, including creation, delivery, modification, suspension, and removal of user identities.

title: Authentication information
text: Authentication information is allocated, managed, and protected so that it is not disclosed, tampered with, or lost during its lifecycle.

title: Access rights
text: Access rights to information and assets are provisioned, reviewed, modified, and removed in line with the access control policy and job requirements.

title: Information security in supplier relationships
text: Processes and procedures are established to manage information security risks in the use of supplier products or services.

title: Addressing information security within supplier agreements
text: Relevant information security requirements are established and agreed with each supplier that accesses, processes, or manages the organization's information or assets.

title: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain
text: Processes are defined and implemented to manage information security risks associated with products and services provided by the ICT supply chain.

title: Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services
text: Supplier services are monitored, reviewed, and managed to maintain agreed levels of information security and address identified deficiencies.

title: Information security for use of cloud services
text: Processes for acquiring, using, managing, and exiting cloud services are established in line with information security requirements.

title: Information security incident management planning and preparation
text: The organization plans and prepares to manage information security incidents consistent with the information security policy and with severity-based response.

title: Assessment and decision on information security events
text: Information security events are assessed and a determination is made whether they should be classified as information security incidents.

title: Response to information security incidents
text: Information security incidents are responded to consistent with documented procedures.

title: Learning from information security incidents
text: Knowledge gained from information security incidents is used to strengthen and update the organization's controls.

title: Collection of evidence
text: The organization establishes and applies procedures for identifying, collecting, acquiring, and preserving evidence for any resulting legal action.

title: Information security during disruption
text: The organization plans how to maintain information security at an appropriate level during disruption.

title: ICT readiness for business continuity
text: ICT readiness is planned, implemented, maintained, and tested based on business continuity objectives and ICT continuity requirements.

title: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements
text: Legal, statutory, regulatory, and contractual requirements are identified, documented, and kept up to date for each information asset.

title: Intellectual property rights
text: The organization implements procedures to protect intellectual property rights and to protect material holding critical or valuable information.

title: Protection of records
text: Records are protected against loss, destruction, falsification, unauthorized access, and unauthorized release.

title: Privacy and protection of personally identifiable information
text: Privacy and protection of PII is ensured per the organization's obligations under relevant legislation and regulations.

title: Independent review of information security
text: The approach to managing information security, including people, processes, and controls, is reviewed independently at planned intervals.

title: Compliance with policies, rules and standards for information security
text: Compliance with organizational information security policies, rules, and standards is reviewed at planned intervals.

title: Documented operating procedures
text: Operating procedures for information processing facilities are documented and made available to personnel who need them.

title: Screening
text: Background verification checks on all candidates are carried out before joining and throughout employment, proportional to business and security requirements.

title: Terms and conditions of employment
text: Employment contracts and agreements state each person's and the organization's responsibilities for information security.

title: Information security awareness, education and training
text: Personnel receive appropriate awareness, education, and training in information security and update it at regular intervals.

title: Disciplinary process
text: A formal, communicated disciplinary process enables action against employees who commit an information security breach.

title: Responsibilities after termination or change of employment
text: Information security responsibilities and duties are defined and communicated for personnel after termination or change of employment, and remain valid.

title: Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements
text: Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements reflecting the organization's needs protect information and are reviewed at defined intervals.

title: Remote working
text: Information security is protected for personnel working remotely, including protection of equipment, data, and communication channels.

title: Information security event reporting
text: All employees and contractors are required to promptly report observed or suspected information security events through a formal mechanism.

title: Physical security perimeters
text: Security perimeters are defined and used to protect areas that contain information and associated assets.

title: Physical entry
text: Secure areas are protected by appropriate entry controls, and only authorized personnel are admitted.

title: Securing offices, rooms and facilities
text: Physical security is applied to offices, rooms, and facilities in line with risk assessment.

title: Physical security monitoring
text: Premises are continuously monitored with unattended and monitoring equipment to detect unauthorized physical access.

title: Protecting against physical and environmental threats
text: Protection against physical and environmental threats, such as fire, flood, and power loss, is designed and applied.

title: Working in secure areas
text: Procedures are developed and applied for working in secure areas to protect information and assets.

title: Clear desk and clear screen
text: Clear desk and clear screen rules are defined and enforced for physical information and information processing facilities.

title: Equipment siting and protection
text: Equipment is sited and protected to reduce risks from environmental threats, hazards, and unauthorized access.

title: Security of assets off-premises
text: Off-premises assets, including media and equipment, are protected, considering the different risks of working outside the organization's premises.

title: Storage media
text: Storage media, including backup and removable media, is managed and protected throughout its lifecycle.

title: Supporting utilities
text: Utilities supporting information processing systems (power, water, cooling, etc.) are protected against failure and interruption.

title: Cabling security
text: Power and communications cabling carrying data or supporting information services is protected from interception, interference, and damage.

title: Equipment maintenance
text: Equipment is correctly maintained to ensure continued availability, integrity, and confidentiality of information.

title: Secure disposal or re-use of equipment
text: Equipment, and any data stored within it, is verified as sanitized before disposal or re-use.

title: User endpoint devices
text: Information stored on and processed by user endpoint devices is protected.

title: Privileged access rights
text: The allocation and use of privileged access rights is restricted and managed.

title: Information access restriction
text: Access to information and application system functions is restricted in line with the access control policy.

title: Access to source code
text: Read and write access to source code, development tools, and software libraries is managed appropriately.

title: Secure authentication
text: Secure authentication technologies are implemented to enable an organization to verify the identity of users and systems.

title: Capacity management
text: The use of information processing resources is monitored, adjusted, and projected to meet system performance requirements.

title: Protection against malware
text: Protection against malware is implemented using appropriate management controls and detection techniques.

title: Management of technical vulnerabilities
text: Technical vulnerabilities in information systems are identified, evaluated, and remediated in a timely manner.

title: Configuration management
text: Configurations are established, documented, implemented, monitored, and reviewed to ensure the security of systems and software.

title: Information deletion
text: Information is deleted when no longer required, respecting legal, statutory, regulatory, and contractual requirements.

title: Data masking
text: Data masking is used in line with the organization's access control policy and other topics, taking into account applicable laws.

title: Data leakage prevention
text: Data leakage prevention measures are applied to detect and prevent unauthorized disclosure or transmission of information.

title: Information backup
text: Backup copies of information, software, and systems are maintained and regularly tested per documented policy.

title: Redundancy of information processing facilities
text: Information processing facilities are implemented with sufficient redundancy to meet availability requirements.

title: Logging
text: Logs recording user activities, exceptions, faults, and information security events are produced, stored, protected, and analyzed.

title: Monitoring activities
text: Networks, systems, applications, and users are monitored for anomalous behavior to detect potential security incidents.

title: Clock synchronization
text: Clocks of all relevant information processing systems are synchronized to a single reference time source.

title: Use of privileged utility programs
text: The use of utility programs that could override system and application controls is restricted and tightly controlled.

title: Installation of software on operational systems
text: Procedures are implemented to control and manage the installation of software on operational systems.

title: Networks security
text: Networks and network devices are secured, managed, and controlled to protect information in systems and applications.

title: Security of network services
text: Security mechanisms, service levels, and management requirements of network services are identified, implemented, and monitored.

title: Segregation of networks
text: Groups of information services, users, and systems are separated on networks, including segmentation of management interfaces.

title: Web filtering
text: Access to external websites is managed to reduce exposure to malicious content, and to protect against phishing and malware.

title: Use of cryptography
text: Rules for the effective use of cryptography, including key management, are defined and implemented.

title: Secure development life cycle
text: Rules for the secure development of software and systems are defined and applied.

title: Application security requirements
text: Information security requirements are identified, specified, and addressed when developing or acquiring applications.

title: Secure system architecture and engineering principles
text: Principles for engineering secure systems are established, documented, maintained, and applied to any information system.

title: Secure coding
text: Secure coding principles are applied to software development.

title: Security testing in development and acceptance
text: Security testing of systems and software is planned and carried out during the development lifecycle.

title: Outsourced development
text: Security activities are directed for outsourced software development and the resulting artifacts, in line with the secure development policy.

title: Separation of development, test and production environments
text: Development, test, and production environments are separated and secured, with rules for moving changes between them.

title: Change management
text: Changes to information processing facilities and systems are subject to formal change management controls and procedures.

title: Test information
text: Test information is appropriately selected, protected, and managed, and operational data is not used in test systems.

title: Protection of information systems during audit testing
text: Audit tests and assurance activities are planned, approved, and agreed between the tester and appropriate management.
